title: IgA Nephropathy and IgA Vasculitis HSP Nephritis: Oxford Classification and Care
subject: ss-paediatric-nephrology
module: Glomerular Diseases, Nephrotic Syndrome and Nephritis

steps.say: Macroscopic hematuria occurring concurrently with upper respiratory infections represents the hallmark of childhood IgA nephropathy.
steps.tx: Identify the timing of clinical presentation to recognize **Synpharyngitic macrohematuria hallmark** in affected children. IgA nephropathy typically presents with recurrent episodes of gross macroscopic hematuria developing concurrently (within twenty-four to forty-eight hours) with an upper respiratory tract infection (synpharyngitic hematuria). This timing sharply contrasts with acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, where macroscopic hematuria and nephritis develop after a prolonged latent interval of one to three weeks.

right.title: Post-Streptococcal GN (Post-Infectious)
points: Profound transient depression of serum C3

steps.say: The multi-hit hypothesis delineates how galactose-deficient antibodies form pathogenic immune complexes that deposit in mesangium.
steps.tx: Review molecular pathophysiology to grasp the **Galactose-deficient IgA1 multi-hit hypothesis** underlying disease progression. Pathogenesis involves elevated circulatory galactose-deficient IgA1 (Hit 1), generation of anti-glycan autoantibodies (Hit 2), subsequent circulating immune complex formation (Hit 3), and mesangial immune deposition triggering mesangial cell proliferation, inflammatory cytokine release, and podocyte injury (Hit 4). These events drive progressive glomerulosclerosis and interstitial fibrosis.

steps.say: Biopsy scoring utilizing the Oxford MEST-C classification accurately predicts long-term renal survival and guide therapy.
steps.tx: Utilize renal histopathology to apply the **Oxford MEST-C histopathological scoring** on renal biopsy specimens. The revised Oxford classification scores M (mesangial hypercellularity in over 50% of glomeruli), E (endocapillary hypercellularity), S (segmental glomerulosclerosis), T (tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis in over 25% of the cortex), and C (cellular or fibrocellular crescents in any glomerulus). These validated histological features predict renal outcome independently of clinical variables.

steps.say: Optimizing renin-angiotensin-aldosterone blockade forms the mandatory initial supportive intervention for all proteinuric patients.
steps.tx: Enforce rigorous conservative treatment through **First-line supportive RAAS inhibition** before considering systemic immunosuppression. For persistent proteinuria exceeding 0.5-1.0 g/day/1.73m² (or spot UPCR > 0.5-1.0 mg/mg), maximum tolerated angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin receptor blocker therapy is recommended for at least ninety days prior to considering immunosuppression. Tight ambulatory blood pressure control and dietary sodium restriction are simultaneously mandated.

vis.title: First-Line Supportive Care in IgA Nephropathy

steps.say: Targeted-release formulation of budesonide acts directly on mucosal Peyer patches to suppress pathogenic IgA1 production.
steps.tx: Deploy gut-directed anti-inflammatory therapy using **Targeted-release oral budesonide (Nefecon)** in high-risk pediatric and adolescent cases. Targeted-release oral budesonide (administered at sixteen milligrams daily, designed to deliver active drug selectively to the distal ileum mucosal Peyer patches) significantly reduces galactose-deficient IgA1 synthesis, lowers proteinuria, and slows estimated glomerular filtration rate loss in high-risk progressive IgA nephropathy while minimizing systemic corticosteroid toxicity.

vis.title: Targeted-Release Budesonide Profile
rows: Markedly reduced systemic glucocorticoid side effects

steps.say: IgA vasculitis manifests with a distinctive clinical tetrad dominated by dependent non-thrombocytopenic purpura.
steps.tx: Recognize multi-system involvement through the **IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein purpura) tetrad** in presenting children. IgA vasculitis presents with the classic tetrad of non-thrombocytopenic palpable purpura (characteristically distributed across dependent lower limbs and buttocks), arthralgia or non-erosive arthritis, colicky abdominal pain (with risk of gastrointestinal bleeding and intussusception), and glomerulonephritis manifesting with hematuria and variable proteinuria.

steps.say: Extensive crescentic formation on renal biopsy mandates immediate immunosuppressive therapy to rescue kidney function.
steps.tx: Institute aggressive rescue protocols for **Crescentic HSP nephritis intervention** to arrest rapidly progressive renal failure. Renal biopsy showing crescents in over fifty percent of glomeruli in IgA vasculitis nephritis warrants immediate aggressive therapy with intravenous pulsed methylprednisolone (thirty milligrams per kilogram per dose, maximum one thousand milligrams daily for three consecutive days) followed by oral glucocorticoids and intravenous cyclophosphamide.

nodes.label: IV Pulsed Methylprednisolone (30 mg/kg/day x 3 days)

steps.say: Systematic longitudinal urinalysis surveillance detects occult nephritis during the initial six months post-vasculitis.
steps.tx: Establish rigorous outpatient follow-up through **Urine screening surveillance in HSP** across all pediatric presentations. All children diagnosed with IgA vasculitis require serial blood pressure measurements and urinalysis screening weekly for the first month, then every two to four weeks for at least six months. This protocol ensures early detection of late-onset nephritis, allowing prompt intervention before irreversible sclerotic damage ensues.
